sections.h2: How can I sell a house fast in DeSoto?
sections.html:
In DeSoto the options are an agent listing, a sale you run yourself, or a sale to a cash buyer who accepts the house unrepaired. The cash route gives up some price in return for speed.

DeSoto is in southern Dallas County, and the city's own materials describe it that way. That puts your property tax with the Dallas County tax office and the Dallas Central Appraisal District, and it puts a lot of local rules into the city's code enforcement office. Two of those rules, rental registration and short-term rental permits, come up often when an investor looks at a DeSoto house.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, and brings showings plus a wait on the buyer's loan.
  • Do it yourself: you skip the commission and take on every form.
  • Cash buyer: a shorter timeline with no repair list, at less than a staged, repaired house might bring.

sections.h2: Does DeSoto require rental registration if my house is tenant-occupied?
sections.html:
Yes. DeSoto's Rental Registration and Inspection Program applies to every residential rental, including single-family houses, duplexes, multi-family buildings, townhomes and manufactured homes.

The city says the ordinance was adopted on February 23, 2021, charges $10.00 per unit, and requires each unit to be inspected every year. Registration itself does not have to be renewed each year if tenants and ownership have not changed. Inspections are scheduled with the city, an inspector needs the tenant, owner or a representative present, and only exterior inspections take place without advance notice. Registration runs through the city's Civic Access Portal, with a paper form by appointment with Code Enforcement at 469-658-3067.

If tenants live in the house you are selling, a buyer will want proof that registration is current and the last inspection passed. Open violations tend to lower offers. The city's program page also says some data in its new portal may be incomplete, and asks owners to report a missing property by email or by leaving a detailed message with the rental registration line, with replies Monday through Thursday between 8:30 am and 10 am and up to two business days to answer.

sections.h2: Can a DeSoto house be used as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Only an owner-occupied one-family or two-family dwelling, and only with a registered permit. The city defines a short-term rental as overnight lodging for one to twenty-nine days, and says the operator must not provide food or beverages.

The program also has a complaint line. Neighbors who see noise or parking problems at a short-term rental can use the city's online portal or call 800-685-1699, and the city says it is monitored around the clock. Once approved, the operator gets a permit number by email that must appear in advertisements and on booking sites.

Ordinance No. 2180-19 requires every operator to register and obtain a permit. The city lists a $125 annual fee per property and warns that failing to register can bring a citation with a fine of up to $500 per day. The application needs a sketch floor plan with room dimensions and a site plan showing the maximum number of vehicles that can be parked on the property without blocking streets, sidewalks or alleys. Operators also collect and remit occupancy tax monthly.

A buyer who wants a short-term rental cannot count on the rule fitting their plans, so send them to the city before they commit.

sections.h2: How does Dallas County property tax work for a DeSoto seller?
sections.html:
The Dallas Central Appraisal District sets the value, and the Dallas County tax office collects. The city's FAQ says DCAD appraises at full market value, must reappraise each property at least once every three years, and mails notices in May for properties reappraised that year.

If you disagree, the FAQ describes an informal meeting with an appraiser first, then a formal protest to the Appraisal Review Board. It also says exemptions cost nothing to file, and that you should contact DCAD if a company asks you to pay to file one. Taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after January 31, when the state requires penalty and interest.

Texas statewide, the Comptroller says schools give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption and owners 65 or older get an added $60,000 school exemption. DeSoto's other taxing units may add their own. Ask the county tax office what is on your bill.

  • Ask for the current-year payoff amount well before closing.
  • Confirm your homestead exemption is on file.
  • Keep your last tax statement for the title company.

sections.h2: What if my DeSoto house is inherited, in default or tax-delinquent?
sections.html:
Each situation runs on its own deadline, and a sale can still work if you move before it expires. A Texas will can be probated within four years of death. If there is no will, a small estate affidavit is available when the estate meets the State Law Library's tests, including a $75,000 asset limit not counting homestead and exempt property.

On a defaulted mortgage the lender must give notice of default, and you can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days. Auction notice follows after that, with the sale itself falling on a first Tuesday. Dallas County sets the sale area, so ask the county clerk where notices are filed.

For delinquent property tax, Texas lets you ask for a penalty and interest waiver in writing before the 181st day after the delinquency date, provided the tax is paid within 21 days of learning of it. Ask the Dallas County tax office for the account history first. The city's FAQ lists the county's Customer Care Center at 214-653-7811 for tax questions, and the Dallas Central Appraisal District at 214-631-0910 for appraisal and exemption questions.

faqs.q: What is the DeSoto rental registration fee?
faqs.a: The city's program page lists $10.00 per unit, with each side of a duplex counted as one unit. Each unit also needs an annual inspection.

faqs.q: What is the fine for an unregistered short-term rental in DeSoto?
faqs.a: The city says a citation can carry a fine of up to $500 per day. Registration is $125 per year for each property.
The Dallas Central Appraisal District. The city's FAQ says it appraises at 100 percent of market value and reappraises each property at least every three years.

faqs.q: When are DeSoto property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after January 31, according to the city's FAQ. Texas then adds penalty and interest.

faqs.q: Do buyers need DeSoto's approval to rent a house they buy?
faqs.a: They need to register it. A long-term rental falls under the rental registration program, and a short-term rental needs its own permit and must be owner-occupied.
